entries.short_title: Wilson yucca direct lights and skyglow recruitment
entries.screening_reason: 2019 California 5 original sites x 3 transects each, randomly assigned 8 directly lit and 7 control transects. 60 chosen yucca plants, 2 without blooms excluded, fruit set analysis n=58 plants. Adult-moth light trap is a separate 6th site/crossover experiment. Ambient skyglow is an observational gradient. Original fruit model has positive illuminance coefficient but 85-percent CI only, treatment coefficient not robust; effect scale, fruit denominator and transect-level covariance unverified.
entries.note: This is ONE published study with a directly manipulated fecundity component; published Wilson 2020 thesis chapter 2 is source overlap not second experiment. Original species Hesperoyucca whipplei pollinated by diurnal Tegeticula maculata maculata, not observed nocturnal moth dependence; do NOT code V=0 without day/night exclusion.

entries.short_title: Xiao Elsholtzia field ALAN phenology fruiting inflorescences
entries.screening_reason: 2025 Biological Conservation ORIGINAL field ALAN × animal-exclusion 40 plots (4m2 each). Reproduction measured fruiting INFLORESCENCE COUNT, not initially tagged flowers with mature seeded fruit; budding/flowering/fruit/seed maturation earlier 3.4–6.2 d; fruiting inflorescences lower under ALAN. Animal exclusion is NOT established to be diurnal/nocturnal pollinator exclusion; independent ALAN installation unit and treatment-cell means/SE not recovered. Authentic official Elsevier supplementary DOCX 315350 bytes SHA256 verified, but contains THREE supplementary figures, ZERO numeric tables.
entries.note: Genuine light manipulation with negative reproductive-capacity direction, but original source has no day-only/open night dependency V. Published phenology is competing direct physiological/temporal mechanism, not proven moth pollen loss. Do not conflate 40 plots with 40 independent lamp units.

entries.short_title: Grognuz Knop light slug factorial seed set
entries.screening_reason: Direct experimental 3-night light pre-exposure plus herbivory factorial; one daylight 90-min pollination observation per target inflorescence. Preprint Table S3 provides 448 pot target frames, 425 recorded seed counts and 28 choice blocks; derived block-balanced light/dark seed ratios ~0.714 in two species, but independent lamp treatment unit is not 28, plants reused, 23 missing seed outcomes, and nocturnal access dependence V unmeasured.
entries.note: Original source author model beta -0.40 p=.014; new block-balanced mean ratios are descriptive not model reanalysis. This study isolates nighttime exposure carryover to daytime pollination. Cannot be used as nocturnal pollinator channel loss. Block-derived CSV not raw author data.

source_audit.source_stage: Public author supplementary Table S3 visible as PDF-reproduced HTML. Derived 28x4 block-level mean and count data were manually transcribed from original Table S3, and reproduced source published treatment means. Original public author Mendeley raw files still inaccessible.
source_audit.response: seed count per standardized target flower/inflorescence after 90 min daytime visitation; target flowers bagged during preceding three illuminated nights
source_audit.treatment: 2x2 ALAN / dark (3 nights) x slug / no slug; pots shuffled into 28 choice blocks each 16 pots (4 each treatment)
source_audit.independent_lamp_assignment_units: Not reconstructable from published block table; field lights shared across cages and repeated calendar weeks. Twenty-eight daytime choice blocks are not independent installations.

original_author_seed_model.scale: author link-scale model β; not pooled simple logRR

source_audit.interpretive_counterexample: Observed ALAN-associated decline in reproduction after all night pollinators were excluded from target flowers during pre-exposure; subsequent pollination only daytime. Challenges 'only nighttime insect-dependent plants suffer ALAN' necessity statement, not evidence that species cannot use nocturnal pollination in nature.
